title: Daulat Khan Reports Hindustan's Disorder to Babur

blocks.text: After initial difficulty reaching the conqueror, Daulat Khan was given audience with Babur and finally able to speak about conditions in Hindustan. He lays before Babur the secrets of Delhi and the weakness of the Lodhi-Pathan establishment, turning private grievance into a full political briefing.

His complaint is that misrule has become structural rather than accidental. Experienced officers and wazirs were slain or discarded, while immature and incapable men were elevated into posts that required judgment, discipline, and strategic sense.

The page then sharpens that complaint with proverbial force. Rai Bhoi's warning that small men cannot accomplish great tasks becomes the moral of the courtly diagnosis, explaining why the kingdom has become vulnerable to an invader who knows how to seize opportunity.
